metabolites_reported: Glycolic acid; Fumaric acid; Arachidonic acid; Caprylic acid; Dodecanol; Iminodiacetic acid; Trihydroxypyrazine NIST; Pyrazine 2,5 dihydroxy NIST; 2 hydroxyvaleric acid; Dihydroabietic acid; Phytol; 2 hydroxybutanoic acid; Aspartate
association_with_blood_pressure: All 13 metabolites significantly associated with HCTZ BP response in whites (DBP and SBP p-values <0.05, q-values <0.05). SPTLC3 rs6078905 genetic variant and sphingomyelins (N24:2, N24:3, N16:1, N22:1) also associated with BP response.
association_direction: Positive association: rs6078905 C-allele carriers show better BP response (ΔSBP −11.4 vs −6.8 mmHg; ΔDBP −6.9 vs −3.5 mmHg). Negative correlation: higher baseline sphingomyelins linked with larger BP drop.
main_findings: Thirteen metabolites from Table S1 significantly associated with HCTZ BP response in PEAR whites. Integrated analyses identified SPTLC3 rs6078905 as predictor of superior BP response. Sphingolipid metabolic pathway implicated in HCTZ mechanism. Baseline sphingomyelins (N24:2, N24:3, N16:1, N22:1) inversely correlated with BP response.
population_size: PEAR whites n=228 (primary analysis); PEAR blacks n=148 (replication); GERA whites n=196 (replication); lipidomics subset n=40 females
